newsitem.title: USA: Scores of Californians sickened by illegal cheese.
newsitem.headline: Scores of Californians sickened by illegal cheese.

text.p: State health officials said Tuesday that about 90 people have fallen ill in central California in recent weeks after eating illegally produced soft cheese and they urged consumers to be wary.

The victims were sickened by salmonella bacteria in Santa Clara and San Mateo counties, which cover an area south of San Francisco and around San Jose, the California Department of Health Services said.
The illnesses were reported over the last six to eight weeks and everyone had recovered without need for hospitalization, a department spokesman said.
They fell ill after eating illegally produced, soft, "Mexican-style" cheeses bought from door-to-door sellers, street vendors and flea markets, the department said.
"These cheeses were apparently produced illegally by unlicensed manufacturers," Frank Nava, an official with the department's food and drug branch, said.
"Since the cheeses were made in unregulated facilities, the cheeses may have been made with unpasteurized milk or manufactured in unsanitary conditions leading to contamination," he added.
Nava said consumers should buy soft fresh cheese only from markets and should check to ensure it was in a sealed container with a lot code or a "pull from sale" date.
Symptoms of salmonella-caused illness include abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, vomiting, fever and headache which begin six to 48 hours after eating contaminated foods.
The Santa Clara and San Mateo county health departments have been working together to find the source of the cheeses causing the illnesses, the department of health services said.
Investigators found a facility in San Jose that was manufacturing cheese and other food products without a license and under extremely unsanitary conditions, it said.
Samples were taken for testing, which is still going on, and the food products were destroyed, it said. A criminal investigation by state and local authorities is still under way, it added.
